newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' PNB workers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' PNB workers call off strike.

text.p: The Philippine National Bank's labour union said on Wednesday it had called off its strike after the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) issued a return-to-work order.
"We did not defy the DOLE order. We have returned from the picket line and called off the strike," Jerry Tan, president of the Philnabank Employees Association (Pema) told Reuters.
"Everybody returned to work as early as yesterday noon when the DOLE order was issued," said Mila Llorin, PNB spokeswoman.
PNB said the labour department has assumed jurisdiction over the issues being discussed by the company and the labour union.
On Tuesday, PNB employees went on strike over a dispute with the bank's management on which union officials could be part of the wage negotiating panel.

Llorin said the DOLE is expected to arrive at a decision on the issue within three months. Tan said of the union's 6,500 members, some 4,500 took part in the strike. PNB has a total workforce of 7,500.
But PNB said its branches were open on Tuesday and only about 100 persons had joined the picket in front of the bank's main office in Manila.
